newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SocGen-Crosby sees rebound in Hong Kong stocks.
newsitem.headline: SocGen-Crosby sees rebound in Hong Kong stocks.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks have taken a hit from an absence of foreign liquidity, but capital inflows should return once uncertainty about property prices and interest rates dissipates, SocGen-Crosby said on Tuesday.
"At the moment the market is definitely at attractive valuation levels," economist Clive McDonnell told reporters.
He maintains a year-end target for the blue chip Hang Seng Index of 15,000 points and an overweight position in Hong Kong on a regional basis.
The Hang Seng Index closed at 12,398.57 points on Tuesday, up 110.73 compared with Monday's close.
McDonnell said Hong Kong had suffered from a capital outflow during the first quarter of the year.
Rate uncertainty and fears of a slowdown in the property market had diverted attention away from the key drivers of the market, such as earnings growth and economic growth, he said.

"Since the introduction of the Real Time Settlement System in December of last year... there has been definitely an oversupply of new short-dated Exchange Fund bills that has put downward pressure on interest rates and in my view is resulting in a capital outflow taking place in Hong Kong at the moment."

Under the Real Time Gross Settlement System, banks can use government Exchange Fund bills and notes to obtain interest-free intraday liquidity by carrying out intraday repurchase transactions with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).
McDonnell said the HKMA was making efforts to reduce the oversupply.

"Once that is completed, it will allow buyers to start entering into the market and provide some support to equity values," he said, adding that Hong Kong should benefit from asset allocation increases and inflows of liquidity from China.
McDonnell said investors needed to form a consensus view about the outlook for interest rates and the property market.
"I think once these factors come to pass, then you will see the market come to life again."

McDonnell said investors would then be able to focus on earnings and economic growth. SocGen-Crosby forecasts earnings per share growth of 12.9 percent for Hang Seng Index companies and Gross Domestic Product growth of 5.4 percent in 1997.
It expects the U.S. Federal Reserve to follow up on a 25 basis point rise in the federal funds rate in March with another quarter percentage point tightening in the second quarter.
"Subsequent to that we don't anticipate further tightening," said McDonnell.
He said SocGen-Crosby was also expecting seven to eight percent capital appreciation in the local real estate market.

McDonnell said SocGen-Crosby was focusing on conglomerates which were expected to generate three-year compound annual growth rate of 20.7 percent at the core level. "This sector will definitely outperform on a 12-month view," he said.

McDonnell said SocGen-Crosby was also overweight in property developers. Although it has cut its core earnings per share growth forecasts for 1997 to 14.2 percent from 26.5 percent, it has upgraded 1998 growth to 25.9 percent from 17.3 percent.
"The main reason for the change related to the timing of the booking of earnings and exceptional items as opposed to any major change in the outlook for the sector," it said.
SocGen-Crosby has a neutral position in banks due to their "tremendous outperformance over the past seven months" and a neutral position in utilities.
